title: Nutrition and Parkinson's
content: A balanced diet can support general health and wellbeing for people living with Parkinson's disease. Eating a variety of nutritious foods and maintaining adequate hydration can support overall health. Fiber and fluids can be particularly relevant when managing constipation. Nutrition needs can differ between individuals, especially when swallowing difficulties, weight changes or other medical conditions are present. Food can also affect the absorption or timing of some Parkinson's medications, including levodopa, so medication and meal timing should be discussed with a healthcare professional when relevant. Dietary advice should complement medical care rather than replace prescribed treatment.
